2027-03-17.title: Wednesday of the sixth week of the Great Fast · St Patrick
readings: Rebekah at the well: “I will draw for your camels also”
Be imitators of God, as beloved children
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me”
2027-03-17.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), sixth week. Commemoration of St Patrick, bishop, apostle of Ireland.
2027-03-17.verse: Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
theo: God answers the servant's prayer at once: “Before he had finished speaking, there was Rebekah,” coming out with her water jar on her shoulder. He runs to her and asks for a little water. Watch how she answers: “Drink, my lord,” she says, and “quickly” lowers her jar; then, without being asked, “I will draw for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.” She empties her jar into the trough and runs again to the well, again and again, until all ten camels have drunk. The text is full of her speed: quickly, ran, quickly. Her generosity is not measured; it goes to the end. The servant “gazed at her in silence,” and when he learns that she is of Abraham's kindred, he bows his head and worships: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his steadfast love and his faithfulness toward my master.” Origen loved this scene. He noted that Rebekah came to the wells every day, and that is why the servant of Abraham found her there; so the soul that comes daily to the wells of Scripture will meet the messenger of the Bridegroom (in substance).

Paul tells us whose generosity Rebekah reflects: “be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.” Christ did not give a measured love; he gave himself, to the end, and that self-offering is made present on our altar in every Holy Qurbono. In the Gospel, Jesus goes to the synagogue at Nazareth “on the sabbath day, as was his custom,” and reads from Isaiah: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives.” Today we remember St Patrick, who knew captivity from the inside. Seized from Britain by raiders at about sixteen, he spent six years as a slave herding flocks in Ireland, and there, he tells us in his Confession, he learned to pray many times a day and through the night (in substance). He escaped, became a priest and bishop, and then did the most Christ-like thing: he went back to the land of his slavery to bring the people who had enslaved him the good news of release. That is what it means to be an imitator of God.
outline: Ask: when did someone do more for you than you asked?
Point 1 · I will draw for your camels also
Rebekah's generosity goes to the end.
Christ gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering.
Patrick returns to the land of his slavery.
“Be imitators of God, as beloved children.”
live: Today, when someone asks you for a small help, do the whole job, gladly and without being asked twice.
Think of one person who hurt you, and do one kind thing for them or pray for them by name, as Patrick did for Ireland.
2027-03-17.prayer: Lord God, you answered the servant's prayer before he had finished speaking and showed him Rebekah's generous heart. Make us imitators of you, as beloved children, living in love as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us. By the prayers of St Patrick, who returned with the gospel to the land of his captivity, give us courage to bring good news to the poor and release to captives, and to love even those who have wronged us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Christ “gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God”; the same offering is made present on the altar of the Holy Qurbono.

quick: Rebekah gives water to the servant and, unasked, to all his camels; the servant blesses God.
Be imitators of God and live in love, as Christ gave himself up for us.
Jesus reads in Nazareth: the Spirit has anointed him to bring good news to the poor and release to captives.
2027-03-17.action: Do one task today more fully and gladly than you were asked.
2027-03-17.question: Is my generosity measured, or does it go to the end?

family.explain: A young woman named Rebekah came to the well. A tired traveller asked her for a drink. She gave him water, and then she said: I will give water to your camels too! She ran back and forth again and again until all ten camels had enough. God was pleased with her kind heart. Today is also the day of St Patrick, who brought Jesus to Ireland.
family.intention: We pray for the people of Ireland and for all missionaries.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we help tomorrow, even if they do not ask us?”

illus: Every summer, outside a small shop near the bus stand in Adoor, an old man sets up a water booth, a thanneer panthal: a clay pot, a few steel tumblers, sometimes buttermilk with ginger and curry leaves. He does not ask who you are or what you believe. Drivers, schoolchildren and labourers stop to drink. When asked why he does it, he said: when I was a boy I walked to school in the heat and a woman gave me water every day. I never knew her name. This is my way of paying her back.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us before we finish speaking. Make us imitators of you, as beloved children, and fill us with your Spirit to bring good news. Amen.
share: I will draw for your camels also (Genesis 24:19). Where can I give more than I am asked?
Live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us (Ephesians 5:2). What does it mean for me to give myself, not only my things?
He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives (Luke 4:18). Who around me is a captive, to fear, addiction or loneliness?
pm.resp: Lord, make us imitators of you.
interc: For the Church in Ireland, and for all Irish missionaries who served in India.
For people in slavery and trafficking today, that they may be set free.
For all who serve strangers with no hope of return.
For missionaries who have returned to difficult places to preach the gospel.
For the grace to love and pray for those who have hurt us.
pm.close: Father, St Patrick returned to the land of his captivity with the good news of your Son. By his prayers make us generous like Rebekah, loving like Christ, and bold to bring release to captives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God answers prayer quickly. Before the servant had finished speaking, there was Rebekah (Genesis 24:15). He asks for a little water. She says: Drink, my lord. Then, without being asked: I will draw for your camels also, until they have finished drinking (Genesis 24:18–19).
Ten thirsty camels! She runs to the well again and again. Her generosity does not stop halfway. That is what God's love is like, and what our love should be like.

Paul says: be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us (Ephesians 5:1–2). Christ did not give a little; he gave himself, and he gives himself still in the Holy Qurbono.

Today we remember St Patrick. He was taken as a slave to Ireland when he was a boy. He escaped, became a priest and bishop, and then went back to the same land to bring them Jesus. Like Jesus in Nazareth he brought release to the captives (Luke 4:18). May we also love even those who hurt us. Amen.
kids: Children, Rebekah gave water to a tired man, and then to all his ten camels! That is a lot of running. When Mummy asks you to help with one thing, try doing two. And remember St Patrick: he went back to the people who had made him a slave, to tell them about Jesus. That is real love.

intro: Theme: “Be imitators of God, as beloved children.”
On the memorial of St Patrick: Rebekah's generosity, Christ's self-offering, and the good news brought back to the land of captivity.

points.h: I will draw for your camels also
q: She opens her hand to the poor, and reaches out her hands to the needy.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Do one small help today fully and gladly, without being asked twice.

sub: Christ gave himself up for us.
A fragrant offering on the altar.
q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
I give you a new commandment, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.
points.apply: Give one hour of your time this week to someone who cannot repay you.

sub: Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth.
Patrick the bishop who went back.
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
And how are they to proclaim him unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who hurt you, and look for a way to do them good.

concl: Rebekah's generosity went to the end; Christ's love went to the Cross.
Patrick carried the good news back to those who had enslaved him.
2027-03-17.resolve: Live in love as Christ loved us, and bring good news even to those who have wronged us.
